facts.f: Russia is the largest country in the world by area.
facts.e: It stretches across Europe and Asia and has 11 time zones.

facts.f: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world.
facts.e: It lies inside the city of Rome in Italy and is smaller than many parks.

facts.f: Tokyo is the capital of Japan. Japan's money is the yen.
facts.e: Japan is a country made of thousands of islands.

facts.f: Beijing is the capital of China. China's money is the yuan, also called renminbi.
facts.e: The Great Wall of China runs across the north of the country.

facts.f: Washington, D.C. is the capital of the United States, not New York.
facts.e: The US money is the dollar.

facts.f: London is the capital of the United Kingdom. Its money is the pound sterling.
facts.e: The River Thames flows through London.

facts.f: Paris is the capital of France, which uses the euro.
facts.e: The Eiffel Tower stands in Paris.

facts.f: Canberra is the capital of Australia, not Sydney.
facts.e: Canberra was specially planned to be the capital.

facts.f: Ottawa is the capital of Canada, not Toronto.
facts.e: Canada is the second-largest country in the world by area.

facts.f: Brasília is the capital of Brazil.
facts.e: People in Brazil speak Portuguese. It is the largest Portuguese-speaking country.

facts.f: Nepal's flag is the only national flag that is not a rectangle or a square.
facts.e: It is made of two stacked triangles, showing a moon and a sun.

facts.f: Japan's flag is white with a red circle in the middle.
facts.e: The red circle stands for the Sun. Japan is called the 'Land of the Rising Sun'.

facts.f: Bangladesh's flag is green with a red circle placed a little towards the flagpole.
facts.e: Dhaka is the capital of Bangladesh, and its money is the taka.

facts.f: Switzerland's flag is a square: a white cross on a red background.
facts.e: Vatican City is the only other country with a square flag.

facts.f: Canada's flag has a red maple leaf on white, between two red bands.
facts.e: The maple tree is a symbol of Canada.

facts.f: The euro is the shared money of many European countries.
facts.e: Euro coins have one side common to all and one side designed by each country.

facts.f: The Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt was built about 4,500 years ago.
facts.e: It was built as a tomb for the pharaoh Khufu.

facts.f: The Great Wall of China cannot be seen from the Moon with the naked eye.
facts.e: This is a popular myth. The wall is very long but quite narrow.

facts.f: Sri Lanka has two capitals: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte and Colombo.
facts.e: Parliament is in Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte; Colombo is the biggest city and business centre.

facts.f: Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal and Thimphu is the capital of Bhutan.
facts.e: Both countries are India's neighbours in the Himalayas.

facts.f: Indonesia is made of more than 17,000 islands.
facts.e: It is the largest country made entirely of islands.

facts.f: Berlin is the capital of Germany.
facts.e: From 1961 to 1989, the Berlin Wall divided the city into two parts.

facts.f: Rome is the capital of Italy.
facts.e: Vatican City, a separate country, is inside Rome.

facts.f: Cairo is the capital of Egypt. It lies on the River Nile.
facts.e: Cairo is one of the biggest cities in Africa.

facts.f: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya.
facts.e: Kenya is famous for its wildlife parks and long-distance runners.

facts.f: South Africa has three capital cities.
facts.e: Pretoria is for the government, Cape Town for Parliament, and Bloemfontein for the Supreme Court of Appeal.

facts.f: Mexico City is the capital of Mexico.
facts.e: It was built on the site of Tenochtitlan, the old Aztec capital.

facts.f: Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina.
facts.e: Its name means 'good winds' or 'fair winds' in Spanish.

facts.f: Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia. Its money is the riyal.
facts.e: Saudi Arabia is mostly desert.

facts.f: Abu Dhabi is the capital of the United Arab Emirates. Its money is the dirham.
facts.e: Dubai is the UAE's biggest city, but not its capital.

facts.f: Singapore is a city-state: a country that is a single city.
facts.e: It is an island at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula.

facts.f: Ankara is the capital of Türkiye (Turkey), not Istanbul.
facts.e: Istanbul is the biggest city and lies partly in Europe and partly in Asia.

facts.f: Seoul is the capital of South Korea. Its money is the won.
facts.e: Korea is famous for its alphabet, called Hangul.

facts.f: Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan.
facts.e: It was built as a new planned capital in the 1960s.

facts.f: Naypyidaw is the capital of Myanmar.
facts.e: It replaced Yangon as the capital in the 2000s.

facts.f: The flag of the USA has 50 stars and 13 stripes.
facts.e: The stars stand for the 50 states and the stripes for the first 13 colonies.

facts.f: Amsterdam is the official capital of the Netherlands.
facts.e: But the government and parliament sit in The Hague.

facts.f: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand.
facts.e: It is the southernmost national capital in the world.

facts.f: Bangkok is the capital of Thailand. Its money is the baht.
facts.e: Thailand was never colonised by a European power.

facts.f: Chile is a very long and narrow country in South America.
facts.e: It is more than 4,000 km long but on average less than 200 km wide.

facts.f: Moscow is the capital of Russia.
facts.e: The Kremlin, a famous fortress, is in the heart of Moscow.

facts.f: Madrid is the capital of Spain, and Lisbon is the capital of Portugal.
facts.e: Spanish and Portuguese explorers sailed across the world in the 1400s and 1500s.

facts.f: Kabul is the capital of Afghanistan and Tehran is the capital of Iran.
facts.e: Both countries have mountainous landscapes.

facts.f: Male is the capital of the Maldives, a country of coral islands.
facts.e: The Maldives is the flattest country in the world: most land is barely above sea level.

quiz.q: Which is the largest country in the world by area?
quiz.x: Russia covers parts of both Europe and Asia.

quiz.q: Which is the smallest country in the world?
quiz.x: Vatican City lies inside Rome.

quiz.q: What is the capital of Australia?
quiz.x: Canberra is the capital, though Sydney is bigger.

quiz.q: What is the capital of Canada?
quiz.x: Ottawa is Canada's capital.

quiz.q: What is the money of Japan called?
quiz.x: Yuan is China's, won is Korea's and baht is Thailand's.

quiz.q: Which country's flag is not a rectangle or a square?
quiz.x: Nepal's flag is two stacked triangles. Switzerland's is square.

quiz.q: Which country's flag has a red maple leaf?
quiz.x: The maple leaf is Canada's symbol.

quiz.q: What is the money of Bangladesh called?
quiz.x: Bangladesh uses the taka.

quiz.q: What is the capital of Brazil?
quiz.x: Brasília became the capital in 1960. Buenos Aires is Argentina's capital.

quiz.q: Which language is spoken by most people in Brazil?
quiz.x: Brazil was once a Portuguese colony.

quiz.q: What is the capital of Türkiye (Turkey)?
quiz.x: Istanbul is the biggest city, but Ankara is the capital.

quiz.q: What is the capital of Nepal?
quiz.x: Thimphu is Bhutan's capital.

quiz.q: What is the capital of Bhutan?
quiz.x: Thimphu is the capital of Bhutan.

quiz.q: Which country has three capital cities?
quiz.x: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.

quiz.q: What is the money of the United Arab Emirates called?
quiz.x: The UAE uses the dirham.

quiz.q: What is the capital of Japan?
quiz.x: Seoul is South Korea's capital.

quiz.q: How many stripes are on the flag of the USA?
quiz.x: 13 stripes for the first 13 colonies; 50 stars for the 50 states.

quiz.q: In which country is the Great Pyramid of Giza?
quiz.x: It was built about 4,500 years ago in Egypt.

quiz.q: What is the capital of New Zealand?
quiz.x: Auckland is bigger, but Wellington is the capital.

quiz.q: What is the money of the United Kingdom called?
quiz.x: The UK uses the pound sterling.

quiz.q: What is the capital of Egypt?
quiz.x: Cairo lies on the River Nile.

quiz.q: What is the capital of the United States?
quiz.x: New York is the biggest city, but Washington, D.C. is the capital.
